name: The Buckingham household at 2036 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_buckingham_e

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 2036 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903) and again in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904), which bracket 1 July 1904. The 1905 list prints: 2036 E. Buckingham & drs.; Clarence Buckingham.

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 2036, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. The 1900 census (ED 40, T623 roll 245) was read for this card. The five live-in staff it lists at the house on 1 June 1900 are on the card, graded inferred because the count was taken four years before the scene. The daughters named in the 1900 census now have individual cards linked from the collective Blue Book entry. Their presence on 1 July 1904 remains uncertain. The 1910 census (T624 roll 241, ED 166 and 167) was read for this card's children: the children it lists, and those the Blue Book lists at the number from 1890 to 1911, are on the card with the years each lived here, whether or not they were at home in 1904. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

persons.name: E. Buckingham
persons.note: The 1900 census lists Ebenezer Buckingham here as head, born January 1829, in Ohio, widowed, president, bank (ED 40, sheet 9A, line 1, leaf n810).

born.note: Biographical date from the cited period publication(s). The earlier census transcription on this card is retained as a separate reading; where it disagrees, this figure uses the independently published biographical date. The publication date is not the date the photograph was taken.

portrait.caption: E. Buckingham, undated photograph published in Men of Illinois (1902), p. 103.
portrait.why: Identified by the printed caption and checked against the household record. The monochrome photograph does not establish skin, eye or clothing colours.

persons.name: The Misses Buckingham
persons.note: The Blue Book prints '& drs.' after the household's name: two or more unmarried daughters at home, neither named nor counted. One line stands for them all. 'Miss Buckingham' is the book's own form of address, not a recorded name. The 1900 census lists the unmarried daughters at home as Kate S. Buckingham (born August 1859, in Ohio, single; ED 40, sheet 9A, line 3, leaf n810); Lucy M. Buckingham (born September 1862, in Illinois, single; ED 40, sheet 9A, line 4, leaf n810). Which of them the 1904 line stands for, the book does not say. The 1910 census names the daughters at home as Kate S. Buckingham, 51, and Lucy U. Buckingham, 40, with their brother Clarence (ED 167, sheet 5B, lines 81-84).

portrait_research.note: An individual portrait has not yet been verified in the period portrait books and Glessner House Museum article archive searched for this project. Any figure shown is a reconstruction, not an attested likeness.

persons.name: Clarence Buckingham

born.note: The existing census transcription gives born November 1854. The transcription flags uncertainty; the year remains provisional.

persons.name: Lizzie Valentine

born.note: The census gives January 1871, age 29 on 1 June 1900.

occupation.note: Written as "Parlor maid" in the occupation column on 1 June 1900.

persons.note: Enumerated on 1 June 1900 in the house, as a servant (parlor maid); born January 1871, in England, came to the United States in 1894, single. Servants changed places often, so this records who worked here in 1900; no source read says whether this person was still here on 1 July 1904. Part of the name is hard to read on the sheet; this is the best reading.

persons.name: Kate Sturges Buckingham

born.note: The family genealogy, p. 61, gives this exact birth date. The inherited 1900 census transcription gives 1859; that disagreement is retained rather than silently harmonized.

persons.note: Kate S. Buckingham is individually named in the 1900 census transcription on the household’s collective daughters card (line 3). The Blue Books still list unmarried daughters in 1904 and 1905 but do not name them. Continued residence is inferred, not individually attested. The inherited census transcriptions disagree on age. The family genealogy gives her birth as 1858-08-03; this is the date used for the figure.

portrait_research.note: No individual portrait verified in the sources searched; the figure is reconstructed.
